patches.entity_key: Past main clause: passé composé → plus-que-parfait
patches.value: main clause (passé composé) + que + dependent verb (plus-que-parfait)

evidence.notes: Tense concordance in indirect speech: the dependent clause verb follows que and shifts to plus-que-parfait. Order pattern inferred from the source example type 'Il a dit qu'il avait fini.'; low uncertainty.

patches.value: main clause (passé composé) + que + dependent verb (imparfait)

evidence.notes: Present recounted in the imparfait: the que-clause verb follows the main clause and appears in imparfait. Pattern inferred from the related expression 'J'ai entendu dire que'; low uncertainty.

patches.entity_key: Past participle agreement with preceding direct object (que)
patches.value: preceding direct object + que + subject + auxiliary + past participle

evidence.notes: The direct object is fronted before the verb and resumed by que, so the past participle comes last and agrees. Based on source examples such as 'la table en marbre que nous avons trouvée'; low uncertainty.
With être the participle is postverbal and agrees with the subject, as in the affirmative form 'Elle est arrivée en retard.'; low uncertainty.

patches.value: affirmative: penser/croire + que + indicative; negative: ne + penser/croire + pas + que + subjunctive

evidence.notes: Negative form places ne before the verb and pas after it, before que, with the subjunctive in the dependent clause; the interrogative form fronts the verb. Supported by the target's own negative_form and interrogative_form fields.
The plural marker -s attaches to the end of the noun while the plural article precedes it, as in 'les maisons' from the transformations 'maison → maisons'; low uncertainty.

patches.value: multiplier + cent + -s (only when not followed by another number)

evidence.notes: The multiplying numeral precedes cent, and the plural -s follows cent only when no further numeral follows, per 'deux cents' vs 'deux cent trois'; low uncertainty.

patches.value: number + mille (invariable); number + million/milliard + -s (when greater than un)

evidence.notes: The number precedes mille, million or milliard; -s is added after million/milliard only when the number is greater than un, while mille stays invariable, per 'deux mille' and 'deux millions'.
In a single clause the conjunction pourvu que stands first and is followed by the subjunctive, per the target's formation 'Pourvu que + subjunctive (single clause)'; low uncertainty.

patches.value: main clause + pourvu que + subjunctive clause

evidence.notes: In the two-clause conditional construction pourvu que follows the main clause and introduces the subjunctive clause, per the target's formation 'Main clause + pourvu que + subjunctive clause'; low uncertainty.
